open_questions: Impact parameter 0.9077 and duration ratio 1.58 imply a grazing/high-b event on a 0.347 R_sun M dwarf; future high-precision photometry/RV can refine density and eccentricity despite good transit-fold count (density penalty ratio persists per stellar_radius tool).

Centroid remains inconclusive (centroid_all not_run/no sector with clear difference image); a targeted ground-based transit on the target coordinates to confirm on-target location will strengthen the planet case versus a faint blend at >99 arcsec (xgboost planet_rank 0.07 low despite planet-like checks).
dossier.public_summary: A 3.2 Earth-radius, 14.4-day flat-bottom dip repeats 3 times steadily with no secondary eclipse, no odd-even difference and no phase-curve, and no nearby star within a TESS pixel can mimic it. The host is a spotted M dwarf but the signal is not at a spin harmonic. The dip is planet-sized and best explained as a transiting planet, pending a centroid confirmation.

reasons.why: Flat-bottom transit shape (-0.6383 strongly disfavours V-shape), no odd/even difference (diff_sigma 0.7533, depth ratio 1.2), no significant secondary (secondary snr 2.333 vs best_brightening_snr 3.714) and no phase-curve signal (amplitude 447 ppm, ratio_to_depth 0.0621, chi2 2.167 dof 9) support planet over stellar eclipsing binary.
No star inside one TESS pixel (21 arcsec) can plausibly cause the 7198 ppm dip and centroid is inconclusive, not off-target, so a background/blend eclipsing binary is not the best explanation.
reasons.value: plausible_within_1px 0, could_cause_within_1px 0, centroid verdict inconclusive but no sector with clear difference image and 14 Gaia stars within 150 arcsec all need >0.0005 eclipse at 99.2+ arcsec

reasons.why: Planet-sized (3.2 Rearth) dip is consistent across 3 transits and 2 sectors, not driven by a few outliers, favouring on-target planet over variability or bad transits.

reasons.why: Star is spotted (amplitude 11173-14708 ppm, false_alarm 9.227744146508594e-41 to 11957 ppm) but dip period is not at a rotation harmonic and fit implies high impact (star_density_penalty 27.57) that does not indicate a transit-shape problem per Rules; stellar-radius check confirms TIC rad 0.347 R_sun duration_ratio 1.58 and rp 3.21 Rearth for TIC model.
